summary: Midday mini-surge from small chatlet fanout causing ephemeral GPU slot starvation and prefetch contention
description: Issue summary: During a midday window (approx. 11:55-12:20 UTC) the customer's dedicated pool observed a sharp drop in processed throughput accompanied by p99 and p50 latency spikes. The pattern correlates to a burst of many short-lived chatlet streams from a tenant service producing high connection fanout. Symptoms look like ephemeral GPU slot starvation plus prefetch eviction pressure, resulting in autoscaler failing to detect steady demand and oscillating allocations. Impact: customer-facing conversational endpoints returned elevated latencies and occasional 5xxs for ~25 minutes; affected Redwood SLA for throughput for this customer. Observed on dedicated pool serving redwood-open-7b and compatible quantized variant.
impact: Reduced throughput and increased p99 latency for customer chat endpoints for ~25 minutes; several requests returned 5xx. Customer reported degraded user experience and temporary service slowdown during peak window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate many short streaming chat connections (~10-30k concurrent short-lived streams) to the customer's routed endpoint using redwood-open-7b.
2) Each stream sends a short prompt (<=32 tokens) and closes after response.
3) Observe autoscaler metrics and GPU slot allocation, and watch prefetch cache size and eviction rate.
4) Reproduces when small-stream fanout + aggressive prefetcher causes NVMe/DRAM churn and allocator heartbeats to lag.
logs:
Logs attached (snippets):
- scheduler: WARN allocator-heartbeat delta=8s (expected <2s) at 2026-03-13T11:58:12Z
- serving-runtime: ERROR attach-failed no-free-slots (pool_id: ded-58) at 2026-03-13T11:58:14Z
- prefetcher: INFO eviction_rate spike from 12/s -> 180/s between 11:57:00Z-11:59:00Z
- autoscaler: INFO scale_decision: shrink due_to_heuristic=false telemetry_gap=22s at 2026-03-13T11:59:05Z
Referenced dashboards: internal/dashboard/dedicated/pool-ded-58, internal/traces/trace-7f3c4c
comments: Aisha Patel (support): Customer reported p99 spike; investigating capacity. Asked SRE to pull pool attach logs.
Marco Rivera (oncall SRE): Noticed allocator heartbeat delays and prefetch eviction surge; running live qps and free-slot telemetry. Suspect short-stream fanout + prefetch growth.
Customer (NimbusDocs CS): We saw a sudden slowdown after a marketing push; traffic shifted to many tiny conversational calls. We can throttle on our side but need guidance on mitigations.
Marco Rivera: Applied emergency mitigation: limited per-tenant concurrent streams to 500 and disabled aggressive prefetch profile for this customer's pool. Monitoring post-mitigation.
Support Engineer (Lena Cho): Customer confirmed service latency returned to normal after mitigation; collecting postmortem action items.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: small-stream fanout caused a high number of ephemeral connections which created high allocator churn and NVMe/DRAM prefetch cache thrashing. Evidence: allocator-heartbeat lag spikes, high prefetch eviction rate, autoscaler telemetry gaps. Root-cause candidates: (A) aggressive prefetching policy tuned for long-lived streams not suitable for huge short-stream fanout, (B) allocator heartbeat and telemetry aggregation was delayed under many short attach/detach events causing autoscaler to misclassify demand and temporarily shrink capacity, (C) background snapshotter IO amplified NVMe contention. Relevant artifacts: pool ded-58 telemetry, trace trace-7f3c4c, slack thread #support-nimbusdocs (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02NIMBUS123).
resolution:
Short-term: 1) Reduced per-tenant concurrent stream limit for NimbusDocs to 500 to prevent runaway fanout (applied 2026-03-13T12:02Z). 2) Switched their pool prefetch profile to conservative (less aggressive KV grow) and temporarily raised min_allocations for pool ded-58. 3) Asked customer to roll out a throttled client patch to smooth spikes.
Long-term actions (follow-ups): A) Autoscaler telemetry hardening to ignore transient heartbeat gaps and add smoothing for short-stream patterns (ENG-3456). B) Add a prefetcher mode that adapts to stream length distribution and per-tenant tail latency (OPS-2891). C) Improve allocator diagnostics and add a test harness for small-stream fanout scenarios.
Status: mitigation restored acceptable throughput; follow-ups created and linked.
notes_for_customer: We implemented an emergency throttle and conservative prefetch mode which restored your service. Please deploy the client throttling patch we provided to avoid recurrence. We will follow up with engineering on autoscaler and prefetch improvements and keep you updated on timelines.
final_remarks: Case remains open until ENG-3456 and OPS-2891 deliverables are scoped and scheduled. Monitoring will continue for 72 hours post-mitigation.
